fix_commit.message: Fix a NULL pointer dereference in the (undocumented) two-argument version of the decimal() extension SQL function. [forum:/forumpost/fa9c2dc83f|Forum post fa9c2dc83f].
fix_commit.author: drh

findings.title: NULL pointer dereference in decimalFunc() when first argument is SQL NULL
findings.message: In decimalFunc(), when the two-argument form of decimal() or decimal_exp() is called, decimal_round(p, N) is invoked before checking whether p is NULL. The pointer p is the return value of decimal_new(), which can return NULL if the first SQL argument is NULL or if memory allocation fails. The NULL check for p appears only after the decimal_round() call (at 'if( p ){'), so any call like SELECT decimal(NULL, 5) causes decimal_round() to be entered with p==0. Inside decimal_round(), the very first meaningful operation dereferences p->nDigit without any null guard, resulting in a crash.
findings.suggestion: Check p for NULL before calling decimal_round(), or add a null guard at the top of decimal_round() itself. The fix chosen was to add 'if( p==0 ) return;' as the second statement of decimal_round(), ensuring it safely returns when passed a NULL pointer.

ground_truth.root_cause: The introducing commit added the two-argument variant of decimalFunc and placed the decimal_round() call outside (before) the existing NULL check on p ('if( p ){…}'). The decimal_round() function itself also lacked a defensive NULL guard, trusting callers to ensure a valid pointer.
